# tgrep runtime

Ash builds tgrep 1.2.3-ash.58629d2.1 from official v1.2.3 commit `58629d208fcb508614b0ce6824bd78197647148f`. [`runtime-lock.json`](runtime-lock.json) fixes the source archive, [`ash-runtime.patch`](ash-runtime.patch), and the shared [ranking](../../crates/file-search/src/ranking.rs) and [directory admission](../../crates/file-search/src/discovery.rs) sources by SHA-256. This release improves managed native watches, periodic content verification, referenced-generation reclamation, request-line bounds and query statistics. Review source and protocol differences before changing the pin.

The v1.2.3 patch rebase retains the upstream bounded socket reader, sibling candidate batches and their final validation, searched-file statistics, count projections, watcher registration and periodic verification. Ash's global result limit extends those query loops rather than retaining the older sequential candidate loop. No complete Ash adaptation module is superseded: filename catalogs/ranking, disconnect cancellation, host ownership, path-first attachment, typed readiness errors and legacy incremental hints remain necessary for the current consumers.

Validated on 2026-10-18 with WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 x64 and Rust 1.98.0: the locked source and patch rebuilt a 14,177,032-byte stripped executable; `just verify ash-tgrep --lib` passed check, 53 real-engine tests (2 manual benchmarks ignored), and all-target warning checks. CLI scan/index regressions covered literal, regex, Unicode, case-insensitive, glob and no-match queries plus writes/reindexing, compared with v1.2.2. An oversized newline-free request was rejected while subsequent requests and parent-EOF cleanup still worked. Resolver tests, script tests and repository dependency checks passed. macOS execution of this upgrade remains pending.

The same source and release profile also rebuilt on Windows x64 (10.0.22631, Rust 1.98.0), producing a 15,157,248-byte executable. `just verify ash-tgrep --lib` passed check, 39 real-engine tests (2 manual benchmarks ignored), and all-target warning checks. The six CLI scan/index scenarios, writes/reindexing, oversized-request rejection and parent-EOF cleanup passed. PE inspection found zero COFF symbols, no debug sections or cached PDB, and retained imports and unwind data. A 34-byte CodeView record contains only the PDB identity and `tgrep.pdb` filename; it does not embed the symbols. Repeated resolution reused the verified executable without rebuilding.

- Source, patch and shared-source SHA-256 values are checked before applying or compiling. Cargo uses `--locked`; build caches are keyed by source, patch, both shared sources, toolchain, target and release debug/strip settings and verify the resulting binary digest.
- Compilation uses a temporary source and target directory, removed on success or failure. The cache retains only the executable, its digest manifest and the build lock. Reusing a verified executable also removes its legacy compiler target directory under the same lock.
- Development, release and Remote packages use the same resolver. Builds require Rust and Git; searches do not download or compile the runtime.
- Packages retain `ash-resources/tgrep/tgrep[.exe]` and the upstream MIT license.
- `ash-tgrep` supervises upstream `serve --shared` and owns each worktree lease. Ordinary directories, unborn repositories and directory subroots use upstream single-directory `serve`. Search correctness, base generations, admission, watchers and delta checkpoints belong to tgrep.
- Ash defaults Git worktrees to managed v2: authenticated namespace/instance requests, OS owner guards, durable operation intent and terminal receipts, versioned views, and reference-aware bounded collection. The default 2 GiB retention target is soft: protected or grace-period objects may exceed it. Fixed advancement requires an explicit rebuild to capture HEAD; adaptive advancement is disabled. Legacy storage is neither imported nor collected. Original v1 behavior remains covered by real-runtime tests.
- Managed filename reads use a version-checked root guard independent of content readiness and participate in final-root drain. The private `managed-identity` helper reuses upstream credential-file validation. `--ash-parent` watches the owning host's stdin lifetime for both managed and single-directory services; owner preparation explicitly binds Ash claims to that host, so EOF releases even incomplete bootstraps, cancels accepted work and waits for authoritative idle shutdown. Other owners still require their OS lifetime proof. Ordinary standalone managed CLI behavior is unchanged.
- The Ash patch supplies the packaging version, `identity` command, path-ordered global `max_results` (1–5001), a shared status file count, consistent candidate statistics and error code `-32002` for invalidated/not-ready snapshots. Permanent errors retain `-32001`. Ash reconciles only the readiness errors within the original request deadline.
- Path-mode attachment publishes a lease and exact generation key before building content. Two bounded content workers prepare bases and overlays in the background, with one reconciliation at a time per worktree; traditional content-mode attachment still waits for the content base to initialize.
- Legacy content overlays retain the admission policy and verified path evidence from the last publication. File hints reopen only the affected files; directory hints discover only their subtrees. Deleted or replaced ancestors retire their former members. Ignore-source changes, tracked-file exemption changes, ambiguous case spellings, overflow and periodic repair require full reconciliation. Admission, visibility and evidence publish together; `last_reconcile.metadata_files_checked` counts checkout files verified in that pass. In-memory membership updates and checkpoint persistence still depend on the view size.
- A metadata-only file catalog belongs to each serving registration and shares its watcher. It applies the shared directory exclusions at discovery and includes hidden, binary and large files under the engine's ignore rules without waiting for content admission. `files/page` returns at most 1,024 paths and a membership epoch; a cursor fails after membership changes. `files/refresh` confirms file discovery independently of content readiness. Ordinary file hints repair only their paths and ancestors; directory hints repair subtrees. Ignore changes, new ignore sources, overflow and periodic reconciliation trigger a full walk. `files/fuzzy` ranks the engine-owned catalog using the checksum-locked shared Nucleo source and returns only the bounded best results.
- Managed filename requests always observe peer disconnect; legacy opt-in `cancellable` filename requests observe peer disconnect before queued work, during metadata discovery, while waiting for catalog repair and during ranking. Aborted walks never publish their partial catalogs. Legacy half-closing clients retain their response semantics. Registration, content refresh and detach retain durable completion and cleanup semantics; blocking filesystem or Git reads finish before their root guard is released.
- Legacy concurrent path attachment and detach share the registration lock. A separate bounded release queue drains final leases outside the repository registration lock and rechecks leases afterward. Final detach waits for all root reads, including discovery and content reconciliation that continued after socket cancellation, before removing the watcher and view. Detach is idempotent for the same view and lease, allowing cleanup retries after a cancelled response without reopening a removed checkout.
- Managed content reconciliation keeps upstream reserved discovery/accounting and evidence reuse; it still walks metadata rather than using the legacy path-hint optimization. Typed management failures preserve commitment and retry information; only known, uncommitted readiness failures are reconciled automatically.
- Upstream source changes are made only in Ash's temporary build inputs and recorded in the patch; the sibling tgrep checkout is read-only. The patch extends the upstream shared and single-directory services rather than introducing another daemon.
- To update the source, create `source.tar.gz` with `git -c core.autocrlf=false archive` at the new exact upstream commit, update `ash-runtime.patch`, refresh the source, patch and shared-source digests, and verify the source build and real-engine integration tests. Preserve LF bytes when archiving on Windows so the same patch applies on every host. The archive is a source snapshot, not a platform executable.
